Indian finance hub eyes dual share model to kickstart public offers: Report
items.content: Indian regulators are currently assessing a new proposal that would allow companies to introduce dual-class shares for listings in both domestic markets and GIFT City. This initiative seeks to invigorate equity market activity in GIFT City, which has faced challenges regarding limited primary market participation. One class of shares would be traded in rupees, while the other would be dollar-denominated, granting foreign investors easier access alongside reduced tax implications.

items.title: Lifting weights reduces muscle loss from obesity drugs
Retraction Note: Detection of anisotropic cosmic structures on a gigaparsec scale
Experimental compound burns fat without sacrificing muscle
items.content: Researchers at UC Berkeley have identified a compound that could transform weight-loss treatment by helping the body burn more energy instead of suppressing appetite like Ozempic and Wegovy. In mice, the compound boosted energy expenditure by up to 18%, improved blood sugar control, reduced liver fat, and promoted weight loss without significant muscle loss. Even more promising, combining it with existing GLP-1 medications produced greater benefits than either treatment alone.

items.title: Scientists tested 212 plant-based foods. Every single one contained fungal toxins
items.content: A new study has uncovered a surprising concern hiding in popular plant-based foods and drinks. Researchers tested 212 vegan and vegetarian products sold in the UK, including meat alternatives, oat milk, almond milk, and soy milk, and found that every single one contained at least one potentially harmful fungal toxin. Known as mycotoxins, these naturally occurring compounds can contaminate grains, legumes, and seeds during farming and storage.
